paragraphs.text: translated by
1. THOU in the house of man this day enkindled worshippest Gods as God, O Jatavedas.
paragraphs.original: समिद्धो अद्य मनुषो दुरोणे देवो देवान्यजसि जातवेदः ।
paragraphs.translit: samiddho adya manuṣo duroṇe devo devānyajasi jātavedaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Observant, bright as Mitra, bring them hither: thou art a sapient and foreknowing envoy.
paragraphs.original: आ च वह मित्रमहश्चिकित्वान्त्वं दूतः कविरसि प्रचेताः
paragraphs.translit: ā ca vaha mitramahaścikitvāntvaṃ dūtaḥ kavirasi pracetāḥ

paragraphs.text: 2. Tanunapat, fair-tongued, with sweet meath balming the paths and ways of Order, make them pleasant.
paragraphs.original: तनूनपात्पथ ऋतस्य यानान्मध्वा समञ्जन्स्वदया सुजिह्व ।
paragraphs.translit: tanūnapātpatha ṛtasya yānānmadhvā samañjansvadayā sujihva |

paragraphs.text: Convey our sacrifice to heaven, exalting with holy thoughts our hymns of praise and worship.
paragraphs.original: मन्मानि धीभिरुत यज्ञमृन्धन्देवत्रा च कृणुह्यध्वरं नः
paragraphs.translit: manmāni dhībhiruta yajñamṛndhandevatrā ca kṛṇuhyadhvaraṃ naḥ

paragraphs.text: 3. Invoked, deserving prayer and adoration, O Agni, come accordant with the Vasus.
paragraphs.original: आजुह्वान ईड्यो वन्द्यश्चा याह्यग्ने वसुभिः सजोषाः ।
paragraphs.translit: ājuhvāna īḍyo vandyaścā yāhyagne vasubhiḥ sajoṣāḥ |

paragraphs.text: Thou art, O Youthful Lord, the Gods' Invoker, so, best of Sacrificers, bring them quickly.
paragraphs.original: त्वं देवानामसि यह्व होता स एनान्यक्षीषितो यजीयान्
paragraphs.translit: tvaṃ devānāmasi yahva hotā sa enānyakṣīṣito yajīyān

paragraphs.text: 4. By rule the Sacred Grass is scattered eastward, a robe to clothe this earth when dawns are breaking.
paragraphs.original: प्राचीनं बर्हिः प्रदिशा पृथिव्या वस्तोरस्या वृज्यते अग्रे अह्नाम् ।
paragraphs.translit: prācīnaṃ barhiḥ pradiśā pṛthivyā vastorasyā vṛjyate agre ahnām |

paragraphs.text: Widely it spreads around and far-extended, fair for the Gods and bringing peace and freedom.
paragraphs.original: व्यु प्रथते वितरं वरीयो देवेभ्यो अदितये स्योनम्
paragraphs.translit: vyu prathate vitaraṃ varīyo devebhyo aditaye syonam

paragraphs.text: 5. Let the expansive Doors be widely opened, like wives who deck their beauty for their husbands.
paragraphs.original: व्यचस्वतीरुर्विया वि श्रयन्तां पतिभ्यो न जनयः शुम्भमानाः ।
paragraphs.translit: vyacasvatīrurviyā vi śrayantāṃ patibhyo na janayaḥ śumbhamānāḥ |

paragraphs.text: Lofty, celestial, all-impelling Portals, admit the Gods and give them easy entrance.
paragraphs.original: देवीर्द्वारो बृहतीर्विश्वमिन्वा देवेभ्यो भवत सुप्रायणाः
paragraphs.translit: devīrdvāro bṛhatīrviśvaminvā devebhyo bhavata suprāyaṇāḥ

paragraphs.text: 6. Pouring sweet dews let holy Night and Morning, each close to each, he seated at their station,
paragraphs.original: आ सुष्वयन्ती यजते उपाके उषासानक्ता सदतां नि योनौ ।
paragraphs.translit: ā suṣvayantī yajate upāke uṣāsānaktā sadatāṃ ni yonau |

paragraphs.text: Lofty, celestial Dames with gold to deck them. assuming all their fair and radiant beauty.
paragraphs.original: दिव्ये योषणे बृहती सुरुक्मे अधि श्रियं शुक्रपिशं दधाने
paragraphs.translit: divye yoṣaṇe bṛhatī surukme adhi śriyaṃ śukrapiśaṃ dadhāne

paragraphs.text: 7. Come the two first celestial sweet-voiced Hotars, arranging sacrifice for man to worship
paragraphs.original: दैव्या होतारा प्रथमा सुवाचा मिमाना यज्ञं मनुषो यजध्यै ।
paragraphs.translit: daivyā hotārā prathamā suvācā mimānā yajñaṃ manuṣo yajadhyai |

paragraphs.text: As singers who inspire us in assemblies, showing the eastward light with their direction.
paragraphs.original: प्रचोदयन्ता विदथेषु कारू प्राचीनं ज्योतिः प्रदिशा दिशन्ता
paragraphs.translit: pracodayantā vidatheṣu kārū prācīnaṃ jyotiḥ pradiśā diśantā

paragraphs.text: 8. Let Bharati come quickly to our worship, and Ila showing like a human being.
paragraphs.original: आ नो यज्ञं भारती तूयमेत्विळा मनुष्वदिह चेतयन्ती ।
paragraphs.translit: ā no yajñaṃ bhāratī tūyametviḷā manuṣvadiha cetayantī |

paragraphs.text: So let Sarasvati and both her fellows, deft Goddesses, on this fair grass be seated.
paragraphs.original: तिस्रो देवीर्बर्हिरेदं स्योनं सरस्वती स्वपसः सदन्तु
paragraphs.translit: tisro devīrbarhiredaṃ syonaṃ sarasvatī svapasaḥ sadantu

paragraphs.text: 9. Hotar more skilled in sacrifice, bring hither with speed to-day God Tvastar, thou who knowest.
paragraphs.original: य इमे द्यावापृथिवी जनित्री रूपैरपिंशद्भुवनानि विश्वा ।
paragraphs.translit: ya ime dyāvāpṛthivī janitrī rūpairapiṃśadbhuvanāni viśvā |

paragraphs.text: Even him who formed these two, the Earth and Heaven the Parents, with their forms, and every creature.
paragraphs.original: तमद्य होतरिषितो यजीयान्देवं त्वष्टारमिह यक्षि विद्वान्
paragraphs.translit: tamadya hotariṣito yajīyāndevaṃ tvaṣṭāramiha yakṣi vidvān

paragraphs.text: 10. Send to our offerings which thyself thou balmest the Companies of Gods in ordered season.
paragraphs.original: उपावसृज त्मन्या समञ्जन्देवानां पाथ ऋतुथा हवींषि ।
paragraphs.translit: upāvasṛja tmanyā samañjandevānāṃ pātha ṛtuthā havīṃṣi |

paragraphs.text: Agni, Vanaspati the Immolator sweeten our offered gift with meath and butter.
paragraphs.original: वनस्पतिः शमिता देवो अग्निः स्वदन्तु हव्यं मधुना घृतेन
paragraphs.translit: vanaspatiḥ śamitā devo agniḥ svadantu havyaṃ madhunā ghṛtena

paragraphs.text: 11. Agni, as soon as he was born, made ready the sacrifice, and was the Gods' preceder.
paragraphs.original: सद्यो जातो व्यमिमीत यज्ञमग्निर्देवानामभवत्पुरोगाः ।
paragraphs.translit: sadyo jāto vyamimīta yajñamagnirdevānāmabhavatpurogāḥ |

paragraphs.text: May the Gods cat our offering consecrated according to this true Priest's voice and guidance.
paragraphs.original: अस्य होतुः प्रदिश्यृतस्य वाचि स्वाहाकृतं हविरदन्तु देवाः
paragraphs.translit: asya hotuḥ pradiśyṛtasya vāci svāhākṛtaṃ haviradantu devāḥ
